issues.description: getIamPolicy failures silently produce PASS findings instead of unknown/error state.
issues.detail: When getIamPolicy raises (e.g. permission denied), the except branch logs and leaves publicly_shared=False, so the check reports PASS for an image whose policy was never read. An auth error becoming a clean bill of health is a security-relevant failure mode. Introduce a tri-state (unknown) or surface the failure explicitly rather than inventing a safe verdict.

issues.description: Name mismatch between PR description (compute_image_publicly_shared) and code/CHANGELOG (compute_image_not_publicly_shared).
issues.detail: The PR body and class commentary reference compute_image_publicly_shared, while the directory, metadata CheckID, class, and CHANGELOG use compute_image_not_publicly_shared. Pick one name and make the tree, CHANGELOG, and description agree. Grep-driven maintenance and reviewers should not have to guess which spec is authoritative.

issues.description: images().list is unfiltered; spec claims only custom images are evaluated.
issues.detail: images().list(project=project_id) returns whatever the project owns with no filter on deprecated state, family, or source. The PR claims this evaluates only custom images, but the code does not establish that precondition. Either apply an explicit filter or document and justify why none is needed, otherwise the check may emit noisy or misleading findings.

issues.description: Bare except Exception swallows all errors, including programmer faults.
issues.detail: Both try blocks catch Exception with no narrowing, so a missing key, type error, or other bug is logged as if it were an API permission error and the loop continues with corrupted state. Narrow the handlers to the anticipated API exceptions and let unexpected ones surface so failures are not silently masked.

issues.description: Image listing is sequential, inconsistent with the threaded pattern used elsewhere in compute_service.py.
issues.detail: Every other resource collection in this service uses __threading_call__ over projects/regions/zones, but _get_images iterates project_ids serially. Either match the surrounding style or document a specific reason not to. A small extracted _is_publicly_shared(project, name) helper would also let the listing loop read as a clean filter.

issues.description: Test for the IAM-policy exception path asserts PASS rather than the security-relevant failure mode.
issues.detail: Fixture image 3 triggers an exception in getIamPolicy and the test simply asserts publicly_shared is False. The most consequential failure mode (unknown policy reported as PASS) is never exercised at the check layer. Add a check-level test that asserts the desired behavior when IAM is unreadable.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the patch is small and follows the surrounding check pattern, but is not ready to merge. The dominant concern, raised by all three reviewers, is that a getIamPolicy failure silently yields a PASS finding — an auth error becomes a clean bill of health, and the tests lock in that behavior. Naming drift between the PR description and the actual directory/CHANGELOG must be reconciled, exception handling needs to be narrowed, and the unfiltered images().list does not match the stated precondition about custom images. Threading consistency and data-shape concerns are secondary but worth addressing. Verdict: needs work before merge.
